summary.intent: Reduce the context cost of the monokl code-search CLI for agent workflows. This meant first measuring cost against an rg-based policy, then finding a leaner default output shape.
summary.outcome: A cost harness PR (#109) was opened, showing monokl's median output (~10 KB) is about 7x the rg-policy median. A sweep found rows past rank 3 hold 91% of the bytes, and a lean-default-output PR (1 snippet line, relevance cut at 0.3 x top score, floor 3, cap 15) was started, stacked on #105. That PR was not yet finished.

repo: `just agent-cost` (scripts/agent-cost.py) is a deterministic report-only harness that imports rg-compare.py. Its policy and baseline numbers are recorded as section 45 of docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md.
Checks used: `just agent-cost`, `just rg-compare`, `just typos`. `just ci` and Rust tests were not run for the harness PR because no Rust source changed.

Baseline over 222 rows: monokl median 10,012 bytes vs rg-policy 1,463; p90 13,351 vs 12,078. monokl wins on p90 for held-out questions and held-out Rust, and where rg can't locate the file (react-hook-form 13/14 vs 3/14).
The `questions` set is 78% answerable, below the 0.8 threshold, so 9 FAIL markers print. This is the baseline, not a regression.

Bytes per row: snippet 50%, signature 20%, path 12.5%, score/kind/parent/lines ~14%. Rows past rank 3 are 91.3% of default bytes, and 67% of those fall into a waste class (same-file repeats, repeated parents, test/example paths, types paths).
The expected declaration ranks 1st for 173 rows, within top 3 for 204, within 5 for 211, within 8 for 213, and never for 5.
Snippet lines = 0 fails because variable and type rows have no signature, so their declaration text appears only in the snippet (identifiers fall to 15 of 59).

Truncated output ends with `totalCount: T` and a `help[1]` hint. `--max-results` and `--max-tokens` exist, but there is no `--offset`/cursor, no snippet-lines flag and no relevance-cut flag. The hint does not name a flag.
Stacking order: the lean-output PR sits on #105's branch because it touches snippet and row-selection code that #105 and #107 also changed.
workflow: Subagent reports are treated as unverified model output. The assistant relayed the numbers while noting it hadn't re-run them.
Read-only experiments (sweeps, prototypes) came before shipping a default change, and the scripts were cleaned up afterward.
A change to default output affects every search, so it gets its own PR with an explicit `**Breaking:**` note, with the old behavior reachable via flags.
The harness's rg policy assumes the agent already knows where to look, which understates rg's true cost. Comparisons should be read with that caveat.

friction: The cost harness subagent added a CONTRIBUTING.md row outside its stated file ownership (harmless but out of scope).
The offline sandbox blocked fetching origin; the needed branch happened to already exist locally.
Snippet-lines had to be prototyped via an env var because no flag exists.
The harness measures bytes and answerability only, so it cannot show model correctness or the value of usage context in extra snippet lines.
open_items: Finish and merge the lean-default-output PR (`--snippet-lines`, `--min-score`, relevance cut 0.3 x top, floor 3, cap 15). It must stay within 1 question loss per set, report new median/p90 bytes and show no bench slowdown over 2%.
Make the truncation hint name the flag to use.
Add `--offset` or a cursor so asking for more doesn't re-pay the first N rows (documented as a known gap).
Pending merges: #105 (first, since the lean-output PR is stacked on it), #109, and release PR #97. CI on #109 was pending.
Raise `questions` answerability above the 0.8 threshold to clear the 9 FAIL markers.
Evaluate model correctness and the value of usage context beyond bytes and answerability.
